newsitem.title: USA: Fla. jury to mull punitive damages in GM suit.
newsitem.headline: Fla. jury to mull punitive damages in GM suit.

text.p: A jury will return to court Wednesday to decide punitive damages that General Motors Corp must pay in connection with a 1991 accident that left a woman severely brain damaged.
The same jury on Dec. 20 awarded $25.4 million to the family of Therese Hunter, 45, who formerly lived in Jacksonville and now lives in a Miami assisted living center.
The compensatory damage award far exceeded the $15 million to $21.5 million requested by Hunter's attorneys for her medical care.

Hunter was driving her sons, aged 11 and 12, to a swim meet on March 3, 1991, when a truck struck her 1990 Chevrolet Astro van and pushed it into a concrete light pole. The impact dislodged the van's steering column and rammed it into her jaw and skull.
The jury found that General Motors, which made Hunter's van, was responsible for her crippling injuries and the pain and suffering of her two sons and her former husband.
The jury made the $25.4 million award to her father and caretaker, Jesus Carmona. Her sons, who live with their father in Live Oak, Florida, were awarded $25,000 and her former husband $3,500.

Though the trial lasted eight weeks, Circuit Judge Lawrence Fay has said he will restrict the punitive damage phase to three days, Wednesday through Friday. He has forbidden attorneys from commenting on the case until its conclusion.
